name: Rebecca Kassay
bottom_line: The page is largely grounded in real, checkable events, and nothing tested was false. The problems are framing and precision, not fabrication.
findings: Credit inflation on big numbers. The $6.5M Mill Pond Dam figure is the total state commitment; $2.75M was already committed by the Governor before Kassay's $3.75M budget add. Formula school aid (e.g., $282.7M for Longwood) is listed under "Rebecca Delivers" though it flows by statewide formula.

One legislative claim overreaches. The cannabis bills Kassay introduced govern licensed retailers and local zoning input. The bill targeting illicit cannabis (A10698) was sponsored by another member; Kassay co-sponsored it.
One volunteer number is higher than her own office reported: "over 100 smoke detectors" on the page vs. "nearly 100" in 74 homes in her office's release.
Omitted outcome: the Port Jefferson–Rocky Point football advocacy is listed without noting the merger was denied and Port Jefferson fielded no varsity team in 2026.

19 grant line items ($10K–$180K) have no public paper trail. Where one exists it sometimes shows less: Port Jefferson schools ($50K found vs. $130K claimed) and Comsewogue ($48K found vs. $96K claimed).
page_issues: Shared grants are repeated under up to six community tabs, so a reader tallying the page will double-count.
The same grant is described differently in different tabs (Port Jefferson $130K; Three Village $150K).
Two SCPD grants ($20K e-bike enforcement; $40K Behavioral Health Unit and e-bike enforcement) may describe the same money.
None of the ~60 claims link to a bill, release, or budget document.
follow_ups: FOIL the Assembly Ways and Means Committee for the AD4 legislative-initiative / SAM grant list for SFY 2025-26 and 2026-27.
Pull NYSED enacted-budget school aid runs (BT2526, BT2627) for Longwood, Middle Country, Comsewogue, Port Jefferson and Three Village.
Ask grant recipients to confirm receipt and amount.
